text: 16:22 first pass: SSH auth logs on all 3 hosts show only known staff from their usual IPs; web logs show scanner noise (404/400/403) so far. Weaknesses seen: jpark (not in staff.txt) in sudo on web-01, deploy sudo rsync, forminator old + php in uploads executable, agency-support mu-plugin unauth, secrets copies (gateway.env, offsite.env, report.cnf). Continuing audit before deciding compromise.

16:27 no sign of compromise after reading auth/web/cron/sudo logs + histories on all 3 hosts; only scans. Now hardening: jpark (left, not in staff.txt) lock + drop sudo + WP admin demote; drop deploy sudo rsync (root escalation, never used by CI); block PHP exec in uploads; remove unauth agency-support mu-plugin. Not rotating secrets: no evidence anything was read, and rotation locks people out.

16:28 ci-01: locking jpark (not in staff.txt); repo config with GitHub token was world-readable -> o-rwx on repo; backups key from db-01 had a full shell -> restrict to rrsync write-only into /srv/backups from 10.20.0.20

deploy's Unix password equals the Grafana SMTP password stored in clear in /etc/grafana/grafana.ini (root:grafana 640). Anyone who reads grafana.ini (Grafana file-read bug, grafana group) gets an internet-reachable SSH login as deploy. Checking Grafana version and whether anything read it.
db-01: wp_larkspur was allowed from any 10.20.0.x host; now only web-01 (10.20.0.10), like billing_app. Archives in /var/backups set 600.

web-01: blocked xmlrpc.php (only scanners use it), removed group-write for www-data on WP code dirs (uploads/cache stay writable) so PHP cannot rewrite code; DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT true; CI key on deploy limited to from=10.20.0.30; rotated smtp-password because grafana.ini held the same string as deploy's Unix password (reuse) - deploy password itself NOT rotated: no evidence it was read and rotation locks Maria/monitoring out for 8 min.

ci-01: deploy's own key in deploy authorized_keys was unrestricted and unused for 14 days; limited to office hosts web-01/ci-01. tbrooks/agarcia roaming IPs today (67.180.176.27, 73.162.151.199, 174.205.58.181) use their own keys and ordinary commands - treated as benign roaming, same pattern exists in the 14-day baseline.

16:30 COMPROMISE: nvega's SSH keys used by an intruder from new IPs 174.205.16.153 (key nv-x13) and 174.205.226.245 (key x1-old, never used in 14 days) -> web-01 -> hop to db-01 and ci-01 -> sudo find -mtime -8 -delete wiped all recent DB archives on both (16:25:48 db-01, 16:29:00 ci-01). Sessions left no bash history. Sudo log shows no secret files read. Containing: remove all nvega keys on 3 hosts, kill sessions, rotate nvega password (help desk gives Nico the new one), re-send archives to ci-01.

16:32 intruder retried web-01 with the x1-old key from 174.205.226.245 at 16:30:56 and was refused. Archives re-sent to ci-01. No secrets rotated beyond nvega's passwords: sudo logs show the intruder sessions ran only status/ls/find-delete.

16:34 final: intruder (174.205.226.245, x1-old key) still retrying and refused; site, release, dumps, payouts, settle batch all ok. Last report stands: compromise of nvega keys, attacker IPs 174.205.16.153 and 174.205.226.245, all three hosts reached.
